facets.F1_correctness: Adds AuditChainCedarPdp and PdpDecisionAuditChainLogger so each Cedar PDP authorization outcome is signed, hash-chained, durably appended, and replay-verified before the caller receives the decision.
facets.F2_tests: Cargo and Buck2 tests cover signed decision lineage persistence, unsigned prior-ledger startup refusal, attacker-signed prior-ledger refusal, serving signer key-material mismatch, and post-startup untrusted ledger replay mapping to PdpError::AuditChainEmission.
facets.F3_maintainability: The change is a narrow wrapper around the existing CedarPdp and uses the existing de-branded audit-chain-domain and audit-file-adapter crates on current dev rather than adding a second audit-chain implementation.
facets.F4_compatibility: Existing CedarPdp behavior and tenant overlay policy semantics are preserved; the audited wrapper is opt-in via a new type and existing PolicyDecisionPoint callers can continue using CedarPdp directly.
facets.F5_security: Authorization fails closed if signer trust, persisted ledger signature replay, append, or persistence verification fails, preventing unaudited allow/deny outcomes from being used as authoritative decisions.
facets.F6_privacy: Audit payload records only tenant/resource/action/principal identifiers and internal decision lineage needed for replay; no secrets or credential material are persisted.
facets.F7_operability: PdpError::AuditChainEmission gives operators and callers a distinct fail-closed error surface for audit durability failures without broadening the Cedar evaluator path.
facets.F8_performance: The audited wrapper adds local file-ledger replay/append verification only to the explicit audit-chain wrapper path; the default in-process CedarPdp remains unchanged for users that have not enabled durable decision logging.
facets.F9_compliance: The persisted event uses the audit-chain surface authorization.pdp.decision, Ed25519 signature verification, tenant shard replay, and DataClass::Audit/InternalOnly classification to support audit-chain-compatible evidence.
facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is a normal git revert of the PDP adapter/kernel changes and Cargo/Buck dependency declarations; no data migration or generated-face settlement is introduced.
facets.F11_observability: Decision lineage includes decision_id, request_id, tenant_id, principal, resource, action, decision, policy_version, determining policies, and cache-hit state for replay and incident triage.
facets.F13_migration: This ports the previously reviewed AUTHZ-006 dirty-workspace slice onto current origin/dev by binding it to the de-branded audit/core and audit/adapters crates rather than the retired oya/audit-chain crate paths.
facets.M1_challenge_assumption: Rejected broad audit-chain substrate changes because current dev already provides audit-chain-domain and audit-file-adapter under de-branded capability-first paths.
facets.M2_zoomed_out_fit: The change advances the authz/audit north-star while preserving the tenant overlay PDP work already on current dev and avoiding generated JSON, root workflow, or cloud-ci gate edits.

comparable_surfaces: AWS IAM / CloudTrail-style durable authorization decision evidence
Google Cloud Audit Logs for IAM policy decisions
Kubernetes admission/audit trails that fail closed on policy decision uncertainty
hyperscaler_lens.provider_neutrality: Uses local Cedar and Oyatie audit-chain domain/file adapter abstractions; no cloud-provider SDK or external audit service is introduced.
hyperscaler_lens.merge_conflict_resistance: Focused Rust/Cargo/Buck edits under libs/oya-shared-pdp-* plus one append-only evidence record.
hyperscaler_lens.improved_criterion: PDP decisions now have durable signed replay evidence instead of only ephemeral in-memory DecisionAuditRecord values.

scope.summary: Durably emit signed audit-chain-compatible records for shared Cedar PDP decisions.
explicit_non_claims: No generated JSON or generated faces were edited.
No live production rollout or browser/user-story surface is claimed for this library-level change.
No broad authz substrate rewrite, policy-store runtime, or external audit service integration is included.
